title: Auto-subscribe per-cam frame geometry from RTSP, filter noise components in motion gate
summary: V2-094 bumped all 6 cams to native 4K (3840x2160) and 5MP (2560x1920). The motion-gate layer (infra/frame_diff.py + infra/gate.py) was calibrated for 1080p and has been silently suppressing 100% of real alerts since 2026-09-30 17:24 EDT listener restart (2,075 events received 2026-10-01, 0 AI-classified, 0 Telegram delivered). This PRD (1) auto-subscribes each cam's actual delivered frame width/height/fps/format at listener startup via RTSP cap.get() so the gate thresholds are resolution-aware, and (2) replaces the percent-of-frame dilation strategy with a 'filter small components then bridge' approach that scales to any resolution without bridging noise into fake giant blobs.
operator_provided_problem: 2026-10-01: 2,075 Reolink motion events received by listener, 0 AI-classified, 0 Telegram delivered. Last AI-classified alert was 2026-09-30 16:53 EDT, ~30 min before the 17:24 listener restart that loaded V2-094 native-4K bytecode.

Diagnostic on BACK 14:08:41 alert 3855dc19 (Carson drove tractor to workshop): actual pixel-level motion was 157,819 px = 1.9% of frame. compute_cross_diff_bboxes returned bbox=(0,0,3840,2160) = 100% of frame. The motion-gate dilated mask by 22px (1% of min dim), which bridged 153 small noise components across the frame into one giant blob. global_change threshold (60% of frame) then fired and dropped the alert.
Same pattern on FRONT 10:01:10 alert (vehicle arrival): actual motion 3.2% of frame, bbox returned 60-67% of frame, global_change fires.

Operators verbatim 2026-10-01: 'when we subscribe the cameras, we probably need to subscribe the horizontal and vertical image size and that's going to be a big change I think.' / 'OK with waiting for the change to ship before alerts flow again.' / 'idea of having the dependencies set from what the actual frame size sent by the camera is much more elegant.'
Operators verbatim 2026-10-01: '12 pixel sounds small, but maybe it'll work' -- operator accepted the 12px hardcoded cap on survivor-component dilation.

in_scope: Extend infra/camera_creds.py parser to recognize <PREFIX>_WIDTH, <PREFIX>_HEIGHT, <PREFIX>_FRAME_FPS, <PREFIX>_FRAME_FORMAT env keys (graceful fallback to None / 0 if absent)
Add public helper get_frame_geometry(camera_id) -> {width, height, fps, format} | None
Modify infra/frame_capture.py to auto-subscribe geometry from each cam via cap.get(CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH/HEIGHT/FPS) at RTSP open time, write into infra/camera_creds module cache
Log a clear INFO line per cam on subscribe: 'BACK subscribed 3840x2160 @ 2.0fps H265'

Replace infra/frame_diff.py compute_cross_diff_bboxes internals: (a) run connected components FIRST on the raw AND mask, (b) drop components with area < MIN_AREA_PCT * total_pixels (default MIN_AREA_PCT=0.0005 = 0.05% of frame, min_area_px floor of 50), (c) THEN dilate the filtered mask by 12px (HARDCODE, not percent)
Add MIN_AREA_PCT env var (default 0.0005) to .env / .env.example with inline 1-line meaning comment
Add INSIDE_FACING_CAM_LIST and GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT (with per-cam overrides like BACK_GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT) to .env / .env.example
Audit infra/frame_diff.py and infra/gate.py for any other frame-size-dependent constants; document each in PR review
Listener restart verification: after V2-096 ships, restart listener and observe that 2026-10-01-style events flow through to VM1 (no Telegram needed; log lines showing gate=None then vm1=class)
out_of_scope: Camera firmware / Reolink CLI changes (already shipped in V2-094)
Reverting cams from native to 1080p (operator chose to wait for fix)
Modifying infra/vm1_prompt.py or any VM1/VL layer
Auto-discovery via ONVIF (just RTSP cap.get is enough)

design_constraints: Card body size: <=2,500 chars per card (local 35B worker ceiling).
ASCII-clean bodies only (no em-dash, smart quote, arrow, <= glyph).
All new env vars are env-tunable; no hardcoded constants in code. Bool env vars: write what each value does inline.
Backwards compatible: missing width/height/fps in camera-creds.env must NOT crash listener; auto-subscribe fills them.
Listener bytecode is NOT auto-reload. After commit lands, restart listener via launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.farm.surveillance.v2 before runtime verification.
Multi-cam ready: code must handle 6 cams today and N cams tomorrow with no schema change.
Per-cam override env vars: <CAM_ID>_GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT for any cam whose geometry/context requires a different threshold than the default.
Dilation cap is HARDCODE 12px, not percent. Never derive from frame dim. Reason: 12px was correct at 1080p; capping at 12 prevents 4K from bridging noise. Confirmed with operator 2026-10-01.

stories.title: infra/frame_capture.py: auto-subscribe per-cam geometry on RTSP open via cap.get()
scope_files: camera-creds.env (optional: add WIDTH/HEIGHT/FRAME_FPS/FRAME_FORMAT lines as documentation of current subscribed geometry; not strictly required for code to work)
done_evidence: On each RTSP open, after first successful cap.read() or cap.isOpened(), read CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH / HEIGHT / FPS, store into infra.camera_creds._all_cameras[name] dict

If geometry read fails (cap.get returns 0), log WARNING and proceed with width=None / height=None; gate code falls back to actual frame.shape from cv2 frame

Module imports cleanly: `python -c 'import infra.frame_capture'`
Test: unit test that mocks cv2.VideoCapture and verifies get_frame_geometry returns the subscribed values after open
no_go: Do not change RTSP URL paths
Do not block listener startup if a cam is offline; log and skip, retry per existing pattern

stories.title: infra/frame_diff.py: filter noise components, then cap dilation at 12px; infra/gate.py: per-cam GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT
done_evidence: compute_cross_diff_bboxes: (a) compute motion AND mask, (b) run _connected_components FIRST (no pre-dilation), (c) drop any component with area < MIN_AREA_PCT * (frame_w * frame_h) (floor at 50px), (d) THEN dilate the filtered mask by HARDCODE 12px, (e) compute bbox from dilated+filtered
MIN_AREA_PCT env var, default 0.0005 (0.05% of frame), read at call time (no caching)
.env.example: MIN_AREA_PCT=0.0005 with inline comment '# Minimum connected component area as percent of frame (0.0005 = 0.05%). Filters noise.'
infra/gate.py: GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT env var default 60.0, with per-cam override pattern: <CAM_ID>_GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT (e.g. BACK_GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT=85.0)
INSIDE_FACING_CAM_LIST=BACK in .env / .env.example with comment explaining why BACK is treated differently (open garage door = 60-70% normal motion)

tests/test_frame_diff.py: regression test for 'noise at 4K should NOT produce full-frame bbox' (uses synthetic 3840x2160 mask with 100 scattered 50-pixel noise blobs; expects bbox < 5% of frame after filter)
tests/test_gate.py: unit test that per-cam GLOBAL_CHANGE_MAX_PCT override is honored (mock cam_id=BACK with 70% frame bgc, expect gate to pass)
no_go: Do not revert to percent-based dilation
Do not hardcode 12px anywhere except this one location
Do not change the AND mask logic (motion in frame_2->3 AND motion in frame_3->4 is correct)

stories.title: Listener restart + runtime verification: 2026-10-01-style events flow through gate to VM1
done_evidence: After US-096a/b/c commits land on main, listener restart via launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.farm.surveillance.v2
Within 60s of restart, daemon.log shows 6 INFO lines: '<cam> subscribed WxH @ Fps FPS <format>' for all 6 cams
Trigger a synthetic motion event (or wait for one) on BACK cam and confirm: gate_classification != global_change when motion is <60% of frame (use a real backdoor activity)
Confirm: gate passes motion event to VM1 (look for VM1 POST to VISION_LLM_URL in logs)

Test fixture: re-run compute_cross_diff_bboxes on a 2026-10-01 alert that was global_change-suppressed (e.g. 3855dc19) and confirm: with frame geometry auto-subscribed (3840x2160) and MIN_AREA_PCT=0.0005, the returned bbox is < 5% of frame (the actual tractor location), not 100%
no_go: Do not skip the restart step; bytecode reload is required
Do not declare done until the runtime log shows the subscribe lines and a real event flows through

verification_recipe: After US-096a: `uv run python -c 'from infra.camera_creds import get_frame_geometry; print(get_frame_geometry("FRONT"))'` returns dict with width/height keys (or None if not yet populated by auto-subscribe)
After US-096b: `tail -50 logs/daemon.log` shows 6 'subscribed' log lines after listener restart

After US-096c: `uv run python -c 'from infra.frame_diff import compute_cross_diff_bboxes; import numpy as np; from PIL import Image; np.random.seed(0); w, h = 3840, 2160; blank = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8); Image.fromarray(blank).save("/tmp/_a.png"); noisy = (np.random.rand(h, w, 3) * 50).astype(np.uint8); Image.fromarray(noisy).save("/tmp/_b.png"); real = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8); real[1000:5000, 1000:2000] = 255; Image.fromarray(real).save("/tmp/_c.png"); real2 = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8); real2[1000:5000, 1050:2050] = 255; Image.fromarray(real2).save("/tmp/_d.png"); print(compute_cross_diff_bboxes("/tmp/_a.png", "/tmp/_b.png", "/tmp/_c.png", "/tmp/_d.png", w, h))'` returns bbox < 5% of frame, NOT full frame
After US-096d: `tail -200 logs/daemon.log | grep -E 'subscribed|gate_classification|vm1_class'` shows expected pattern for a real motion event
results_interpretation: If US-096d verification shows gate passing real motion to VM1 with bbox <5% of frame (not 100%): V2-096 ships, US-094e observation arc resumes.
If gate still fires global_change on real motion at 4K: diagnose whether MIN_AREA_PCT is too small (noise still getting through), or BACK-specific override not loaded. Iterate US-096c.
If listener fails to subscribe any cam: check infra/frame_capture.py startup order; cv2 may need frame read before cap.get returns valid dims.
